newsitem.title: switzerland: Swiss shares end mixed session weaker.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end mixed session weaker.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swiss shares ended weaker on Wednesday after a session which saw prices fluctuate in a narrow range.
Dealers said the market ran out of steam after a firm opening and turned lower when U.S. data signaled strong economic growth.
Roche, down 25 to 11,825 led the actives list. Novartis, down five to 1,780 ahead of Thursday's first quarter sales figures, was second.
Overall trade volume was 1.88 billion Swiss francs.
Dealers said the market would remain volatile and U.S. data would determine market direction.
Holderbank fell 21 francs to 1,116 reflecting market disappointment over last night's news that the cement producer planned to take provisions totalling 450 million Swiss francs.
Dealers said the the provisions had been too much of a surprise and the company should have given some prior indication to the market about its plans.
Novartis was expected to release good sales figures, one dealer said.
Novartis could profit from a statistical basis effect, one dealer said.
Selected cyclical stocks like Fischer, Rieter, Saurer and Sulzer were firm for most of the session but also came under some pressure when the broad market turned lower.
Banks and insurers suffered from an uncertain interest rate outlook.

UBS, down two francs to 1,322, holds its annual shareholders meeting on Thursday afternoon. But no surprising news was expected after UBS hostile shareholder Martin Ebner said he would not attend the meeting.
Soffex trade was again dominated by roll-overs ahead of Friday's futures expiry. The April future traded around its fair value, dealers said.
Trade in options was quiet with only Roche seeing some activity.
